title: Introduction to Autonomous Systems
description: A foundational overview of what autonomous systems are and how they are designed.
content:
## What Is an Autonomous System?
An autonomous system is a machine or software agent capable of making decisions and acting without continuous human control.

## Core Components
Most systems combine sensing, planning, and actuation. Sensors gather data, planners choose actions, and actuators execute them.

## Real-World Examples
Examples include self-driving vehicles, warehouse robots, and intelligent drone navigation platforms.

title: Perception and Sensor Fusion
description: Covers how autonomous platforms interpret the environment using multiple sensor inputs.
content:
## Why Perception Matters
Perception transforms raw sensor data into usable representations like objects, lanes, and obstacles.

## Common Sensors
Typical sensors include cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS, and IMUs, each with different strengths and weaknesses.

## Sensor Fusion Basics
Fusion combines complementary data sources to improve robustness, especially in noisy or uncertain conditions.

title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
description: Introduces methods used to choose actions when outcomes are probabilistic.
content:
## Uncertainty in Autonomous Environments
Autonomous agents operate with incomplete information, dynamic obstacles, and imperfect models.

## Planning Approaches
Rule-based systems, search algorithms, and probabilistic planners are commonly used depending on task complexity.

## Safety and Reliability
Safe decision-making requires fallback behaviors, confidence thresholds, and continuous risk evaluation.

title: Ethics and Governance in AI Autonomy
description: Examines societal, legal, and ethical considerations in deploying autonomous technologies.
content:
## Ethical Design Principles
Transparency, fairness, accountability, and human oversight are central to responsible autonomy.

## Regulatory Landscape
Standards and regulations vary across sectors, from transportation to healthcare and defense.

## Human-Centered Deployment
Successful systems align with public trust, include clear failure handling, and support auditability.
